content:
The image shows soybean leaves with a distinctive white-to-gray powdery coating covering the leaf surfaces extensively. The coating is uniform and fluffy in texture, clearly coalescing across entire leaf surfaces. The leaves remain green underneath but are heavily blanketed by this powdery growth. Multiple leaves at different positions are affected.

This matches Powdery Mildew precisely: "White to gray powdery patches on leaves that begin small but coalesce to cover the entire leaf as disease progresses" and "White, powdery coating on infected leaves that coalesces to cover the entire leaf."

No other class fits: White Mold presents on stems with black sclerotia; Downy Mildew would show lesions on upper surface with sporulation on underside; this is purely surface powdery growth on leaves.
